hook: A U.S. Air Force MISREP from the 89th Attack Squadron documents an armed reconnaissance mission over Syria on July 30-31, 2022, during which the aircraft crew observed a UAP moving from north to south in under one minute, recorded via dual infrared and electro-optical sensors and submitted to AARO.
why_it_matters: This document is significant as one of the first formally structured AARO submission packages to emerge from a combat theater (Operation INHERENT RESOLVE), demonstrating that the UAP reporting pipeline was operational within USCENTCOM by mid-2022. The explicit 'UAP Signatures: No' field in the structured report form shows AARO had already standardized its intake forms to capture RF and sensor signature data. The observation occurred during an active ISR mission tracking armed personnel and military vehicles, ruling out sensor confusion with friendly or coordinated assets as an explanation.

key_findings.finding: The UAP was observed at 02:39Z on July 31, 2022, lasted less than one minute, and moved from north to south, consistent with the official AARO video description of an object traversing the sensor field of view.

~OBSERVED AN UNIDENTIFIED AERIAL PHENOMENON IVO 37SFU271w'7~(SEE UAP 1).

key_findings.finding: No UAP signatures — including RF frequency or RF duration — were detected by the platform's onboard sensors at the time of the sighting.

The observing aircraft was flying at 19,359 feet altitude and 116 knots airspeed at the time of the UAP contact, providing reference parameters for any relative motion or parallax analysis of the sensor footage.

The mission accumulated over 20 hours airborne with both IMINT and SIGINT collection active, and full-motion video of the UAP event was subsequently exploited by DGS1 (a Defense Ground Station), indicating the footage entered the intelligence exploitation chain.

key_findings.finding: The UAP was observed during an active armed reconnaissance mission under Operation INHERENT RESOLVE, supporting Task Force CHOSIN, with the crew simultaneously tracking ground personnel, armed vehicles, and what may have been weapons systems — context that makes sensor artifact or friendly-asset confusion less plausible.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document is explicitly an AARO submission package — structured with standardized UAP fields and declassified under MDR 25-0094/25-0099 specifically for release to AARO, making it a primary source for AARO's Syria 2022 case file.

The Air Force (AFCENT/USCENTCOM) chain of command and the Defense Ground Station exploitation of FMV represent institutional Air Force ISR infrastructure, though no direct Wright-Patterson connection is named in the document.
